keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1888-1895: the company's administered land as the pages show it, Mombasa. The infobox claims 'an area of about 246,800 square miles (639,000 km2)' along the coast 'from modern Somalia to modern Kenya' and inland to the north-west shore of Lake Victoria; the drawn Mombasa circle is about 1,700 km2, far below that (ratio 0.003), because no page opened says what the company held beyond Mombasa. Buganda is a protectorate in the ledger, not territory.

region.text: Mombasa and its mainland, the company's base ('Mombasa and its harbour were central to operations')

ledger.note: 6 September 1888: the Imperial British East Africa Company is chartered. 'The company was incorporated in London on 18 April 1888 and granted a royal charter by Queen Victoria on 6 September 1888.' It took over the administration of Mombasa from the Sultan of Zanzibar in 1888 (Sultanate of Zanzibar page).

region.text: Buganda, the kingdom whose Kabaka signed the treaty

ledger.note: 1891: Mwanga of Buganda puts his kingdom under company protection. 'The IBEAC sent Frederick Lugard to Uganda in 1890'; 'In 1891, Mwanga concluded a treaty with Lugard', placing 'his land and tributary states under IBEAC protection'. Civil war broke out in Buganda in January 1892 (IBEA page).

31 March 1893: the company leaves Uganda. 'In 1893 the Imperial British East Africa Company transferred its administration rights' to the British government; it 'formally ended its involvement on 31 March 1893'. The Uganda Protectorate was declared on 18 June 1894.

region.text: Mombasa and its mainland, the company's base ('Mombasa and its harbour were central to operations')

ledger.note: 1895: the company's coastal territory becomes the East Africa Protectorate. 'The territory was then divided to form the Uganda Protectorate in 1894 and East Africa Protectorate (later Kenya) in 1895'; the Sultanate of Zanzibar page has the British government proclaiming a protectorate on 1 July 1895 (sentence cut short in the extract opened). The infobox has the company defunct in 1896.

wars.name: Uganda civil war of 1892
wars.outcome: The Protestant and Catholic factions fought for supremacy after the Muslim faction was subdued ('In 1892, having subdued the Muslim faction, the Protestants and Catholics resumed their struggle for supremacy'); 'civil war broke out in January 1892' and Lugard helped build a fort on Kampala Hill. No change of ownership is recorded.
wars.note: Lugard's Maxim gun 'had turned the tide in 1892' (History of Buganda page).

certainty.note: The charter claimed 639,000 km2 with no survey; the 1886 Anglo-German agreement is a spheres line.

sources.title: History of Buganda

sources.title: Uganda Protectorate

sources.title: Imperial British East Africa Company
sources.note: Incorporated 18 April 1888, royal charter 6 September 1888; 639,000 km2; transferred its administration in 1893; Uganda Protectorate 1894 and East Africa Protectorate 1895; defunct 1896.

notes:
New entity (a chartered company, drawn as a colony of Britain; Cliopatria has no row for it and its 'British East Africa' row, 1961-1972, is mis-dated). Pages: Imperial British East Africa Company, Uganda Protectorate, plus the Mombasa and Sultanate of Zanzibar pages.

What is not on the pages: the 1887 concession and its terms (Mombasa page: Mombasa 'relinquished' on 25 May 1887 to the British East Africa Association), the coastal strip leased from the Sultan (not located), Lugard's treaties other than the 1891 one with Mwanga, Kenya's interior. The charter area of 639,000 km2 is a claim; the keyframe is only Mombasa, which understates the company badly, and a gap-filler should open a page on the East Africa Protectorate or the Kenya coast strip. Dates that disagree: charter 6 September 1888 on the IBEA page (the 3 September of other works is not recorded); defunct 1896 (infobox) or the 1895 protectorate.

Counterparts needing dossiers: british-colonial-empire (eu-11), kingdom-of-buganda (this batch), the Uganda Protectorate (1894-1962) and East Africa Protectorate (1895-1920) as colonies (af-08: its 'british-east-africa' row is 1961-1972).
